Dr. Leo does his part in the barn. The next 24 hours are yours.

We see it all the time in North Texas — horse gets adjusted Friday morning, owner hauls three hours to a jackpot that afternoon, and wonders why the change didn't stick. The adjustment is the easy part. What happens after is what locks it in.

Give the horse a light day. Keep water available. Hand walk if you can. Let the body actually use what just got freed up.

This is the difference between a horse that feels good for two days and one that carries the work for weeks.

If your horse is due for a tune-up before summer jackpot season hits, now is the time. Book now — shortgochiro.com or call (406) 799-3369.

Most of the horses Dr. Leo sees in DFW aren't emergency cases. They're horses that have been trying to communicate something for weeks — and the owner finally stopped second-guessing it.

Your horse isn't lazy. She's not being difficult. She's working around something that hurts.

If any of these three show up consistently, it's worth a look. Catching it early is cheaper, faster, and easier on the horse than waiting until she's visibly off.

Dr. Leo is a cAVCA-certified equine chiropractor. He does mobile appointments throughout North Texas — he comes to your barn, no trailering a sore horse.

More wet saddle blankets. More circles. More time. And the problem just gets quieter — not fixed.

Sometimes it is training. And sometimes the horse is doing everything she can with a back that won't cooperate.

Dr. Leo has worked with barrel horses, rope horses, and cutters across North Texas and Montana. He's cAVCA-certified, he comes to your barn, and he tells you straight what he finds.
